term: complete cause contains all productive participants in its effect
definition: CompleteCauseCoversContributors G participants says that, for each complete-cause edge c→e, every member of the independently supplied full participant family for e is a part of c, using existing Covers and the fixed PartialOrder. It does not assert a cause exists.
note: Only the upper-bound consequence of the author’s total/complete participant-sum reading at ChapterVII157/fn211. It is not full Fusion, no-extra-parts, object formation, uniqueness by definition, causal necessitation, or a converse from coverage to causation. Covers alone does not identify an arbitrary set as the actual productive participants; that semantic adequacy remains OPEN. Causing a part does not by this definition make one a participant in causing its whole, and no fixed-family identity across worlds follows.
